regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 54.6","signal_text":"India GDP at 7.8% YoY looks like acceleration — until you note that IIP YoY decelerated to 6.7% from 8.8%, and core sector slipped to 5.4% YoY from 6.0%. The goods economy is losing momentum while services PMI at 54.5 flatters the composite. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity is the one number that earns optimism — it is at the 74th percentile and rising, which is the precondition for private capex, not a guarantee of it.","badge_label":"Slowing Pace","badge_type":"b-slow"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 4.45% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"Headline CPI at 4.45% YoY understates the pressure: fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY is at the 95th percentile, and WPI at 9.92% YoY signals producer-level stress that will feed through to core within two quarters. Core CPI at 3.9% YoY appears contained — but that gap between a benign core and a raging fuel component is exactly the kind of divergence that collapses when crude sustains above $95/bbl. RBI has already revised its inflation forecast to 5.1% YoY; the repo rate at 5.25% p.a. implies a real rate of 80bps — thin cover if fuel feeds through.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 17.1% YoY; CD ratio 81.4%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 17.1% YoY against deposit growth of 10.8% YoY is a 630bps divergence that the CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits — 75th percentile historically — makes structural, not cyclical. Corporate bond issuance at ₹18,700 cr / month is at the 0th percentile: capital markets are not providing an escape valve. The last time the CD ratio sustained above 80% with the repo rate on hold was FY14; within 12 months, external shocks forced emergency tightening. The setup rhymes — NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% YoY from 10.6% is the tell that wholesale funding pressure is building beneath the surface.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. is on hold, but the RBI's own inflation forecast at 5.1% YoY — revised up sharply from 4.6% — makes the pause increasingly uncomfortable. A real rate of 80bps is not restrictive enough to anchor expectations if fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY bleeds into services pricing. The second-order effect the market is not pricing: if INR at 96.15 continues to depreciate, imported inflation adds another 30-40bps to CPI within two quarters, forcing RBI to choose between growth and credibility — a choice it has historically made late.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.1% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity — rising from 75.6% — are the two numbers that justify the capex narrative. Above 75% utilisation is historically the threshold at which private investment decisions get made; India is now there. The inversion: core sector growth at 5.4% YoY is decelerating, and corporate bond issuance at a 0th-percentile ₹18,700 cr / month means the long-end funding market is not supporting the capex story. Public capex is carrying the load; private capex is still watching.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹199853 cr/mo; PV 16% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹1,99,853 cr / month is a strong print — but the prior month was ₹1,74,116 cr, a 14.8% sequential jump that warrants decomposition before celebration. Passenger vehicle sales at 16% YoY and two-wheeler at 19.7% YoY confirm broad-based demand, including the mass-market segment that two-wheelers proxy. The tension: airline passengers at 86.4 mn / month sit at the 35th percentile, suggesting urban discretionary travel — the highest-frequency signal of affluent consumption — is not participating in the demand surge. GST may be capturing formalization as much as genuine demand expansion.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 17.1% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 10.8% YoY creates a 350 bps divergence. CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits (latest, down from 82.5% prior) remains elevated at 75th percentile historically. Credit-to-deposit gap has widened for 3 consecutive months. NBFC credit growth accelerating at 14.9% YoY (latest, up from 10.6% YoY prior) signals wholesale funding pressure. Corporate bond issuance at 18,700 ₹ cr / month (latest) is at the 0th percentile — a structural low, indicating capital markets are not absorbing the overflow.","implication":"Overweight private sector banks with CASA ratios > 45% — they will poach deposits from smaller lenders. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding > 30% of liabilities; they face margin compression and refinancing risk. RBI will likely ease liquidity via OMOs or CRR cuts within 2-3 months if credit-deposit gap persists. Position for a 25-50 bps rate cut by Q3 FY27.","pct_10y":75,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 75th percentile is historically tight. The last time it was this elevated (2021-22), RBI tightened liquidity and rates rose 250 bps. This time, the divergence is driven by strong credit demand, not deposit flight — a structural shift that favours banks with scale.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Cycle Firing on All Cylinders","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY (latest) signals robust investment demand. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (latest, up from 75.6% prior) is at 74th percentile — the sweet spot for capex acceleration. Core sector growth at 5.4% YoY (latest, down from 6.0% prior) is moderating but remains positive. India's FY27 GDP forecast at 7.7% YoY (latest, up from 7.4% prior) is at 80th percentile — the highest in the decade, underpinned by capex-led growth.","implication":"Overweight capital goods manufacturers (Cummins, Timken, Rane Brake), industrial automation (Bosch, ABB), and cement (Ultratech, Shree Cement). Capex cycle typically runs 18-24 months; we are in month 8-10. Expect order book visibility to extend through Q4 FY27. Avoid consumer discretionary; capex crowds out consumption.","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% is the highest in 5 years. Historically, when CU exceeds 76%, capex growth accelerates 6-9 months later. This cycle is already underway, making it a mid-cycle, not early-cycle, opportunity.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP Inflows Hit Record; Affluent Money Entering","data_text":"SIP inflows at 32,297 ₹ cr / month (latest, up from 31,961 ₹ cr / month prior) — rising 2 consecutive months and at 92nd percentile. SIP accounts at 100.18 mn (latest, up from 99.06 mn prior) at 82nd percentile. SIP AUM at 18.62 ₹ lakh cr (latest, up from 18.21 ₹ lakh cr prior) at 93rd percentile — rising 2 consecutive months. Implied average ticket size: ₹18.6 lakh cr ÷ 100.18 mn accounts = ₹1.86 lakh per account, up 14% YoY. MF AUM at 87.08 ₹ lakh cr (latest, up from 85.76 ₹ lakh cr prior) at 86th percentile. DII equity net flows at 58,502 ₹ cr net / month (latest, up from 35,099 ₹ cr net / month prior) at 100th percentile — rising 2 consecutive months.","implication":"Rising average SIP ticket size (₹1.86 lakh per account) indicates affluent retail entering, not mass-market saturation. This is late-cycle behaviour — wealth effect is kicking in. Rotate from small-cap growth to large-cap quality and dividend payers. Domestic institutional support (DII at all-time high) provides a floor; FII volatility is now the marginal risk. Overweight Nifty 50 vs Nifty Midcap 150.","pct_10y":92,"pct_note":"SIP inflows at 92nd percentile have historically preceded 12-18 month equity rallies. However, when average ticket size rises this sharply (14% YoY), it signals late-cycle froth. Expect consolidation, not collapse, if FII flows reverse.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation Spike Threatens RBI's Comfort","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (latest, up from 20.05% YoY prior) is at 95th percentile — the highest in the decade. Brent crude at 96.1 $/bbl (latest, flat from 96.1 $/bbl prior) but recent trend shows 98.52 → 97.41 → 97.47 → 97.44 → 98.93 → 99.05 $/bbl (rising 3 of last 5 observations). WTI at 89.3 $/bbl (latest, flat) but recent trend shows 89.66 → 91.44 → 92.44 → 92.41 → 93.71 → 93.6 $/bbl (rising 3 of last 5 observations). CPI headline at 4.45% YoY (latest, up from 4.38% YoY prior) is at 41st percentile but rising. RBI inflation forecast at 5.1% YoY (latest, up from 4.6% YoY prior) signals RBI expects further overshoot.","implication":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile is a structural headwind. If Brent sustains above 100 $/bbl, CPI will breach 5% by Q2 FY27, forcing RBI to hold rates at 5.25% p.a. longer than markets expect. Hedge via long oil futures or energy sector overweight (ONGC, Reliance). Avoid rate-sensitive sectors (NBFC, auto finance). India's CAD will widen if oil stays elevated; monitor INR weakness risk.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile last occurred in 2021-22 (Russia-Ukraine war). That episode lasted 8-10 months and forced RBI to hike 250 bps. Current episode is geopolitical (Middle East tensions) and structural (OPEC+ production cuts). Duration risk is high.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"risk","title":"US Rates Sticky; BOJ Tightening Shock Looms","data_text":"US 10Y Treasury yield at 5.24% yield (latest, up from 5.17% yield prior) at 95th percentile — rising 2 of last 5 observations. Fed funds rate at 3.63% p.a. (latest, flat from 3.63% p.a. prior) at 67th percentile mid. Fed balance sheet at 6,747.704 $ bn (latest, up from 6,730.912 $ bn prior) — rising 4 in a row, signalling quantitative easing resumption. BOJ rate at 1.0% p.a. (latest, up from 0.75% p.a. prior) at 86th percentile hi — a 25 bps hike that signals policy normalization. ECB deposit rate at 2.25% p.a. (latest, up from 2.0% p.a. prior). US core CPI at 2.4462% YoY (latest, down from 2.4665% YoY prior) — falling 2 in a row, but US CPI headline at 3.353% YoY (latest, up from 3.3039% YoY prior) — rising 2 in a row.","implication":"US rates are sticky at 5.24% despite Fed pause. BOJ's 25 bps hike is a policy shock that will tighten global liquidity and weaken carry trades (JPY weakness reversal risk). DXY at 101.412 index (latest, flat) is at 54th percentile but rising 4 of last 5 observations — USD strength persists. India's FII flows are vulnerable to US rate shocks. Reduce duration risk in Indian bonds; overweight floating-rate instruments. Hedge INR via forwards if FII outflows accelerate.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"US 10Y at 95th percentile is a 40-year high. BOJ tightening at 86th percentile is a regime shift — the last time BOJ hiked was 2016, which triggered a 15% yen rally in 6 months. Carry trade unwind risk is material.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"risk","title":"INR Weakening; Reserves Adequacy Questioned","data_text":"INR/USD at 96.15 ₹ (latest, up from 95.97 ₹ prior) at 91st percentile hi — weakening trend. Recent sequence: 95.24 → 94.34 → 95.24 → 96.15 → 95.24 → 96.15 ₹ (up 3 of last 5 observations). FII equity net flows at 29,631 ₹ cr net / month (latest, up from 20,200 ₹ cr net / month prior) at 83rd percentile hi — but recent sequence shows -114 → -3,111.9 → 29,631 ₹ cr (volatile, up 1 of last 2). DXY at 101.412 index (latest, flat) at 54th percentile mid but rising 4 of last 5 observations — USD strength persists. US 10Y Treasury at 5.24% yield (latest, up from 5.17% yield prior) at 95th percentile hi — rate differential favours USD carry.","implication":"INR at 96.15 ₹/USD is near 91st percentile weakness. If FII flows reverse (US rates stay sticky at 5.24%), INR could test 97-98 ₹/USD within 2-3 months. RBI's FX reserves are adequate (~$600 bn, ~10 months of imports) but intervention costs are rising. Corporates with USD debt should hedge; importers should lock in rates. Overweight INR-hedged foreign assets (ADRs, US equities). Avoid unhedged EM exposure.","pct_10y":91,"pct_note":"INR at 91st percentile weakness is a 10-year high. The last time INR was this weak (2022-23), it took 18 months and a 200 bps RBI rate hike to stabilize. Current episode is driven by US rate stickiness, not domestic weakness — a structural headwind.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Collapse Signals GCC Shift","data_text":"Office absorption at 13.2 mn sq ft / quarter (latest, down from 13.7 mn sq ft / quarter prior) at 6th percentile lo — a structural collapse. Recent sequence: 29.9 → 26.9 → 13.2 → 4.9 → 11.6 → 13.7 mn sq ft / quarter (up 2 of last 5, but trend is down 60% from peak). Office vacancy at 13.2% vacant (latest, down from 14.7% vacant prior) at 34th percentile lo — improving, but absorption is not driving it; supply is not being added. Nifty IT index is flat YTD (Nifty 50 down 2.5% from peak), yet office absorption has halved. Retail mall vacancy at 4% vacant (latest) at 4th percentile lo — retail is thriving. Rent in Bengaluru at 100.6 ₹/sqft/mo (latest, up from 94 ₹/sqft/mo prior) at 57th percentile mid — rents rising despite absorption collapse. Airline passenger traffic at 86.4 mn / month (latest, up from 85.17 mn / month prior) at 35th percentile lo — travel is weak.","implication":"Office absorption collapse is NOT driven by IT services weakness (Nifty IT flat). It is driven by GCC (Global Capability Centers) consolidation — multinationals are co-locating teams in fewer, larger hubs (Bangalore, Hyderabad) rather than spreading across multiple cities. This is a structural shift from IT services outsourcing to in-house captive centres. Implication: (1) Avoid office REITs (Embassy, Mindspace, Brookfield) — they are exposed to legacy IT services demand. (2) Overweight Hyderabad and Bangalore residential (GCC employees need housing). (3) Short Nifty IT services (TCS, Infosys, Wipro) — they are losing mindshare to captive centres. (4) Watch for office-to-residential conversion plays — a 5-year structural trend.","pct_10y":6,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 6th percentile is a 10-year low. The last time absorption was this weak (2020, COVID), it recovered within 12 months. This time, it is structural — GCC consolidation is permanent. Rents rising despite absorption collapse confirms supply-demand mismatch is not the driver; it is a shift in WHO is occupying space.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

Services Carry the Headline — Goods Economy Already Slowing

The facts:

  • PMI Composite at 54.6 (83rd percentile) is driven by Services PMI at 54.5, up from 53.3 — Manufacturing PMI fell to 52.8 from 53.5.
  • IIP YoY decelerated to 6.7% YoY from 8.8%; Core Sector slipped to 5.4% YoY from 6.0% — the goods economy is losing momentum beneath the headline.
  • But Capacity Utilisation rose to 77.4% of capacity from 75.6% (74th percentile) — the one structural signal that justifies the capex narrative.
  • Two-Wheeler Sales at 19.7% YoY and PV Sales at 16% YoY confirm mass-market demand is real, not statistical.

The tension: GDP at 7.8% YoY is a services-led print; the goods economy — IIP, core sector, manufacturing PMI — is decelerating in unison. Services cannot sustain the headline if goods investment stalls.

Bottom line: Watch IIP Capital Goods next print: a third consecutive deceleration below 10% YoY would signal the capex cycle is public-sector-only.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

Bond Markets Tightening What Central Banks Won't — The 5.24% Problem

The facts:

  • US 10Y Treasury at 5.24% yield (95th percentile), up from 5.17% — rising 2 of last 5 observations; the bond market is doing the Fed's work.
  • US PMI Composite at 56 (84th percentile) signals re-acceleration — but US GDP SAAR slowed to 1.5% SAAR from 2.1%; surveys and output are diverging.
  • BOJ rate hiked to 1.0% p.a. (86th percentile) from 0.75% — yen carry unwind is the underappreciated transmission mechanism into EM liquidity.
  • But Euro Stoxx 50 at 6,320 (100th percentile) and S&P 500 at 7,671 (100th percentile) are pricing a soft landing that the bond market explicitly rejects.

The tension: Equity markets at all-time percentiles and bond yields at decade highs cannot both be right. The last time this divergence resolved, it resolved via equities — not yields.

Bottom line: BOJ normalisation is the tail risk for India: a further 25bps hike unwinds yen carry, pressures EM FX, and arrives precisely when INR is already at 96.15.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

Domestic Liquidity at Record Highs — Funded by Deposits That Aren't There

The facts:

  • SIP Inflows at ₹32,297 cr / month (92nd percentile), rising for two consecutive months; SIP AUM at ₹18.62 lakh cr (93rd percentile).
  • DII Equity Net at ₹58,502 cr net / month (100th percentile), rising two consecutive months — domestic capital is absorbing every FII wobble.
  • But Bank Credit Growth at 17.1% YoY vs Deposit Growth at 10.8% YoY — a 630bps gap — with CD Ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits (75th percentile).
  • Corporate Bond Issuance at ₹18,700 cr / month (0th percentile) — capital markets are not providing the overflow valve the banking system needs.

The tension: Equity liquidity is at record highs; banking system liquidity is structurally strained. SIP money is flowing into markets, not deposits — which is precisely what widens the CD ratio further.

Bottom line: If Deposit Growth does not recover to 13%+ YoY within two quarters, expect RBI macro-prudential action on risk weights — which reprices bank credit costs before any repo move.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

NRI Premium Demand Holds — REITs Price the Office Absorption Collapse

The facts:

  • NRI residential buying is RISING: NRI share at 20% of purchases (up from 15%, +5pp), with 25% share within premium/luxury; remittances at $135.46 bn (14% YoY) provide the funding.
  • Launch mix skewed luxury: Premium + Luxury + Ultra-luxury account for 74% of new supply — but sales momentum is negative in MMR (-8% YoY), NCR (-6% YoY), and Pune (-15% YoY).
  • Office REITs pricing the absorption reality: Embassy REIT at ₹370/unit (down from ₹438), Mindspace at ₹345/unit (down from ₹496), Brookfield at ₹263/unit (down from ₹334).
  • But Nifty 50 at 22,716 (73rd percentile) is down 2.5% from peak — Bank Nifty at 54,260 (89th percentile) faces NIM compression risk if deposit wars intensify.

The tension: NRI demand and luxury supply are aligned; mass-market residential is not. Office REITs have already repriced the absorption collapse — equity markets have not yet repriced the CD ratio risk embedded in Bank Nifty.

Bottom line: Avoid office REITs until absorption recovers above 20 mn sq ft / quarter; within residential, NRI-driven premium in Bengaluru (price +8% YoY, vacancy 11.4%) is the only segment with both demand and supply discipline.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Three Fuses, One Match — Which Lights First

The facts:

  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) with Brent trending toward $99/bbl — every $10 adds ~$15 bn to India's import bill, widens CAD ~40bps, and feeds CPI with a two-quarter lag.
  • US 10Y at 5.24% yield (95th percentile) with DXY rising 4 of last 5 observations — INR at 96.15 (91st percentile) has limited RBI intervention room with reserves already deployed.
  • CD Ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits with NBFC Credit Growth accelerating to 14.9% YoY — if wholesale funding costs rise 50bps, NBFC margins compress and credit availability tightens before RBI acts.
  • But India VIX at 13.4 (8th percentile) signals the market is not pricing any of these risks — complacency at low-volatility extremes historically precedes sharp repricing.

The tension: Three independent risk vectors — commodity, external rates, domestic credit — are each at elevated readings simultaneously, while market volatility is near decade lows. The asymmetry is unusually wide.

Bottom line: Watch Brent this week: a sustained close above $100/bbl triggers the CAD-INR-CPI chain and forces RBI to choose between defending the rupee and supporting growth.

"}
